archetypes.name: integration-contracts
archetypes.rationale: The plan makes untested CLI assumptions about dispatch-with-waterfall.sh, aggregate-findings.sh, and /larch:issue batch mode that could invalidate decompose-aggregator.sh's fallback logic and decompose-file-issues.sh's invocation shape before a line is written.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read the actual CLI of `scripts/dispatch-with-waterfall.sh`, `skills/review/scripts/aggregate-findings.sh`, and `skills/issue/SKILL.md` (lines 50–70) to verify that the flags assumed by the plan (`--slots-file`, `--mode description`, `--intra-batch-deps-file`) exist and behave as described. Identify any flag name mismatches, missing parameters, or behavioral differences between what the plan claims and what those scripts currently implement. Pay special attention to the `decompose-aggregator.sh` fallback path — the plan admits `aggregate-findings.sh` may have an incompatible input contract and proposes a single-slot waterfall as fallback; verify whether `dispatch-with-waterfall.sh`'s `--slots-file` NDJSON format is consistent with that single-slot usage. Also confirm that the `/larch:issue` `--no-dedup` / `--intra-batch-deps-file` mutual-exclusion constraint cited at `skills/issue/SKILL.md:59` is actually present at that line number in the current file. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: step-wiring
archetypes.rationale: The SKILL.md replacement claims a single Split-path stub body covers three distinct trigger sources with three different return-to-caller continuations; plan-vs-file drift here would leave one or more trigger paths unreachable or routed to the wrong resumption point.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read `skills/design/SKILL.md` Steps 1c, 1d, and 2b.5 to verify that all three trigger sources (Step 2b.5 hard/soft/`--partition`, Step 1c sprawl, Step 1d sprawl) actually converge on the same Split-path body anchor as the plan claims — confirm the anchor text `#### Split-path (decomposition panel not yet available)` exists verbatim in the current file. Check whether the plan's proposed replacement text accounts for all three distinct return-to-caller paths (Step 2b.5 → Step 3 Gate B; Step 1c sprawl → Step 1d; Step 1d sprawl → Step 1e Gate A) and whether any are missing or mislabeled in the proposed body prose. Verify that `skills/design/references/flags.md` already contains a `## Plan-size thresholds (Step 2b.5)` heading for the plan's proposed ~15-line addition, and that `skills/design/references/plan-review.md` has a bottom section the plan can extend with a cross-reference. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: sentinel-idempotency
archetypes.rationale: The plan introduces two ordered sentinel files for a three-step non-atomic sequence; whether .decompose-issues-filed is written only on full-batch success (not partial) and whether the OOS_FILE_MAP-style format is consistent with file-design-oos.sh's existing sentinel are untested assumptions that affect re-run correctness.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read `skills/design/scripts/file-design-oos.sh` to find the actual sentinel file name, write location, and line format it uses in the `annotate` phase, then compare that against the `OOS_FILE_MAP`-style `PARTITION_FILE_MAP` sentinel format the plan invents for `decompose-file-issues.sh annotate`. Determine whether the plan's `annotate` sub-command writes `.decompose-issues-filed` only after all pieces succeed — or whether a partial-success scenario (`ISSUES_CREATED < ISSUES_TOTAL`) could still write the sentinel, permanently hiding the unfiled pieces from any re-run. Check failure mode 6 in the plan (`ISSUES_FAILED > 0` skips close but does not write the sentinel) against failure mode 7 (sentinel present but `.decompose-original-closed` absent triggers close-only re-run); confirm there is no state where both sentinels are absent yet some issues have already been filed, which would cause duplicate filing on re-run without `/larch:issue`-level dedup protecting against it. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
